summary: Flutamide is a nonsteroidal antiandrogen used in combination with an LHRH agonist for locally confined Stage B2-C and metastatic Stage D2 prostate cancer. The dose is 250 mg every 8 hours (750 mg/day). It carries a boxed warning for severe and sometimes fatal hepatic injury - transaminases must be checked at baseline and monitored, and the drug stopped if ALT exceeds twice the upper limit of normal or jaundice appears.
indications: Locally confined Stage B2-C prostate carcinoma in combination with an LHRH agonist (with radiation therapy)
Stage D2 metastatic prostate carcinoma in combination with an LHRH agonist

dosage.d: 2 capsules (250 mg) three times a day at 8-hour intervals
Start with goserelin 8 weeks before radiation and continue through radiation
dosage.n: Begin flutamide and LHRH agonist together

dosage.d: Initiate with LHRH agonist and continue until disease progression
dosage.n: Do not interrupt LHRH agonist therapy

admin: Take orally; food has no effect on bioavailability
Always give together with the LHRH agonist to prevent disease flare
Measure serum transaminases before starting therapy
Do not start if baseline ALT is more than twice the upper limit of normal
moa: Flutamide is a nonsteroidal antiandrogen that, via its active metabolite 2-hydroxyflutamide, competitively inhibits androgen uptake and the binding of androgens to nuclear androgen receptors in target tissues such as the prostate. By blocking androgen action it counteracts the growth stimulus of testosterone on androgen-sensitive prostatic carcinoma; combined with an LHRH agonist it produces complete androgen blockade.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to flutamide or any component
Women and pregnancy (no indication; fetal harm)
relative: Baseline ALT more than twice the upper limit of normal
G6PD deficiency, hemoglobin M disease or smokers (aniline-type toxicity / methemoglobinemia risk)
monitor: Signs of hepatic dysfunction (nausea, jaundice, dark urine, RUQ pain)

preg: Pregnancy Category D. Flutamide is indicated only in men and may cause fetal harm; it produced feminization of male offspring and reduced offspring survival in animals. It must not be used in women or in pregnancy.
lact: Not applicable - flutamide is indicated only in men. It should not be used by women, including those who are breastfeeding.
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment is established in the labeling. Use general caution; the active metabolite is renally excreted.
hepatic: Contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment. Boxed warning: severe and sometimes fatal hepatic injury can occur. Check transaminases before treatment, monthly for the first 4 months, then periodically; discontinue immediately if ALT exceeds 2x ULN or jaundice develops.

major: Warfarin - flutamide prolongs prothrombin time; monitor INR and adjust anticoagulant dose
moderate: Other hepatotoxic drugs - additive liver injury risk
minor: Drugs causing methemoglobinemia - additive effect in susceptible patients
interactions.food: Food has no effect on flutamide bioavailability; it may be taken without regard to meals.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid heavy alcohol use because of additive hepatotoxicity risk.
interactions.diagnostics: May raise serum transaminases and bilirubin; can elevate plasma testosterone and estradiol; may cause methemoglobinemia.

monitoring: Serum transaminases (AST/ALT) at baseline, monthly for first 4 months, then periodically
Liver function tests at first signs of hepatic dysfunction
Methemoglobin level in patients susceptible to aniline toxicity
counsel: Take the capsules together with your LHRH injection and do not stop without advice
Report at once any yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, persistent nausea, fatigue or right-sided abdominal pain
Your urine may turn amber or yellow-green - this is harmless
Hot flashes and breast tenderness are common; tell your doctor if troublesome
pk: Active metabolite forms rapidly after dosing
2-hydroxyflutamide peaks about 2 hours after an oral dose
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); tight, light-resistant container
pearls: Boxed warning: severe, sometimes fatal hepatotoxicity - check LFTs before and during therapy and stop if ALT >2x ULN or jaundice appears
Always combine with an LHRH agonist for complete androgen blockade; do not use as monotherapy
Most hepatic injury occurs within the first 3 months - monitor closely early
Causes amber/yellow-green urine discoloration - reassure patients
Consider methemoglobin monitoring in G6PD deficiency, hemoglobin M disease, or smokers
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is nearly time for the next 8-hour dose, skip the missed dose - do not double up. Maintaining the every-8-hour schedule keeps androgen blockade effective.
overdose: Signs may include gynecomastia, breast tenderness, raised transaminases and methemoglobinemia. There is no specific antidote and flutamide is not removed by hemodialysis. Induce emesis if the patient is alert and recently ingested, then give general supportive care with monitoring of vital signs and liver function.
